overclaims.statement: Head of Citi's global consumer banking division
overclaims.citedQuote: Fraser is currently head of Citi's global consumer banking division
overclaims.rationale: The cited passage ('Fraser is currently head of Citi's global consumer banking division') is from a September 2020 article describing her pre-CEO role. The dossier marks this claim 'supported' with no staleness flag, presenting a role she left when she became CEO in 2021 as if it were supported current fact; a parallel claim from the same-era CBS source (03de7d32) is correctly marked 'stale', making this inconsistency clear.

overclaims.statement: Global restructuring plan involving 20,000-role reduction announced in September 2023
overclaims.citedQuote: Citigroup had previously announced plans for job cuts in a broad overhaul unveiled in September.
overclaims.rationale: The cited passage says only that 'Citigroup had previously announced plans for job cuts in a broad overhaul unveiled in September.' It gives no headcount figure; the 20,000-role reduction appears invented relative to this citation.

overclaims.citedQuote: Citigroup's Jane Fraser will become the first woman ever to lead a Wall Street bank when she succeeds CEO Michael Corbat in February
overclaims.rationale: The cited passage is forward-looking from 2020 ('will become the first woman ever to lead a Wall Street bank when she succeeds CEO Michael Corbat in February'), an announcement of a future appointment. The dossier marks the resulting role as 'supported' on this citation alone; the passage supports the announcement, not the completed appointment, though other dossier sources do corroborate it.

overclaims.statement: Accomplishments include international business divestitures, hiring new executives, simplifying structure, and regulatory progress

overclaims.rationale: The cited passage says Fraser 'cites as accomplishments' these items — i.e., they are her own self-assessment. The dossier statement converts that self-report into established fact ('Accomplishments include...'), asserting more than the attribution supports.

overclaims.citedQuote: Citi's first female CEO in history

The dossier statement drops the 'Citi's' qualifier, generalizing it beyond what the passage states, though adjacent claims separately support the broader Wall Street first via other sources.

usefulness.rationale: Understanding is strong: the dossier establishes identity (Dame Jane Fraser DBE, b. 13 July 1967, British-American banking executive), her current roles (CEO of Citi since March 2021, chair since October 2025), a full career arc (Goldman Sachs analyst 1988-90, McKinsey partner from 1994, Citi from 2004 through Private Bank, CitiMortgage, Latin America, president of Citigroup, then CEO), and concrete work items (five-core-business strategy, 2023 management shakeup and restructuring, the Transformation, Mexico IPO pivot, net income decline, AI-driven capacity gains, $25M equity award). A reader comes away knowing who she is and what she has done. RemainingQuestions is middling: the status labels (claimed/contested/stale) do flag uncertainty and stale material, but the dossier never explicitly states its gaps or conflicting dates (February vs. March 2021 CEO start appear without reconciliation). ConversationReadiness is high: current title, tenure, recent chair appointment, compensation, strategic priorities, and even her management philosophy (the 'never respond in anger' anecdote) would let a reader prepare for a meeting.
